title: Fracture: quant playbook sketch & onboarding thread
content:
Purpose: rough, portable sketch of a lightweight quant onboarding and rapid-eval checklist the applied-ml team can use when bringing new model variants into Dedicated/Hosted. Meant to be short, pragmatic, and usable by solutions engineers during handoff.

Meeting notes (2027-09-23 sync):
- Quick sync with Maya, Diego, Jonah. Goal: make a 20–30 minute checklist run that yields an initial viability signal (cost & quality) and a follow-up plan.
- Constraints: limited GPU budget for initial probe (<= 2 GPU-hours), want deterministic reproducibility for A/B evaluation across runs.
- Decided on two probe tiers: "smoke" (fast, token-limited) and "survey" (broader, more metrics).

Smoke probe (target ~30m total runtime):
1) Model artifact sanity (5m)
   - verify model loads at target quant config (e.g., 4-bit grouped, per-channel scale).
   - KV cache sanity: feed a 64-token chat history and assert no NV/host OOM.
   - quick perf: tokens/sec on representative microbatch (batch=2, seq=64). Record raw GPU utilization and p50 p95 per-token latency.
2) Tiny eval set (10m)
   - 50 prompt pairs (gold vs expected) across 3 priority tasks: code, summarization, instruction-following.
   - metrics: exact-match-ish where applicable, and embedding-similarity delta (cosine) on outputs for nondeterministic tasks.
3) Cost estimate (5m)
   - extrapolate tokens/sec and token-based cost using Dedicated baseline kernels. Include worst-case memory margin (+20%).
4) Quick QA note (10m)
   - collect 3 example outputs where behavior diverges from fp16 baseline. Short bullet explanation for SE/CS handoff.

Survey probe (target ~2–3h):
- Expanded eval sets (1k prompts across verticals: support, search, code, chat).
- Automatic scoring: BLEURT/ROUGE for generation where applicable, embedding-based MRR for retrieval tasks, repetition/degeneration checks.
- Per-layer activation drift histogram (sampled on 100 examples) vs fp16 baseline to locate layers sensitive to quantization.
- KV cache stress: longer histories (512 tokens) and bursty patterns to trigger eviction/kvc path.
- Per-device perf sweep: run on a small matrix (A100-40, H100-80, RTX8000 emu) — record normalized tokens/sec.

Preflight checklist for Solutions Eng handoff:
- Artifact: model weights, quant config file, tokenizer hash, conversion script commit link.
- Minimal reproducibility script: docker + pinned env + sample eval run (should produce identical metric summary).
- Safety/guardrails notes: any prompt classes showing hallucination increase, sensitive prompt failures, or known tokenization mismatches.
- Suggested fallback routing policy: prefer fp16 for sessions tagged "low-latency/high-accuracy"; allow quant variant as cost-fallback.

Experiment log (notes from quick runs):
- Model: rwd-llm-13b-v2 variant; quant configs: GQA-4 (group size=128) and 6-bit bias-only.
- Smoke metrics (batch=2, seq=64):
   * fp16 baseline: 640 tok/s, p50=9ms/token, p95=16ms/token, mem=11.8GB
   * GQA-4: 1420 tok/s, p50=4.1ms/token, p95=7.8ms/token, mem=7.1GB
   * 6-bit bias-only: 980 tok/s, p50=5.9ms/token, p95=10.5ms/token, mem=9.2GB
- Quality delta on tiny eval (50 pairs): embedding cosine (avg): fp16=0.872, GQA-4=0.854, 6bit-bias=0.865
   -> rough drop: GQA-4 ~2% absolute cosine loss vs fp16. For code tasks EM drop small (~1.1%) but for summarization fluent-ness markers dropped more.
- Noted model-specific fragility: repeated truncation artifacts at end-of-sequence for GQA-4 on long prompts (>420 tokens). Possibly quant-noise interaction with rotary embeddings.

Open questions / to investigate next sprint:
- Is the EOS truncation reproducible across different grouping sizes (64 vs 128)? Priority: high.
- Can we apply per-layer mixed precision (keep first 4 layers fp16) and recover fluent-ness while preserving most performance gains? Medium priority.
- Better embedding deltas: is cosine the right proxy for semantic drift? Should add MR-Score or user-labeled QA delta for a small subset. Low/medium priority.

Action items (owners):
- Diego: run grouping-size sweep (64/96/128) on 10 example long-context prompts and collect token-level alignment traces. Due 2027-09-27.
- Maya: implement minimal reproducibility script + dockerfile and post to GH: redwood-inference/quant-playbooks#312. Due 2027-09-25.
- Jonah: expand tiny eval to 200 prompts (fast-scan) and compute automatic MRR for retrieval prompts. Due 2027-09-28.
- Ava (me): draft short one-pager for SE handoff including suggested fallback routing policy and sample log excerpt. Due 2027-09-29.

Notes-to-self / heuristics we liked:
- Keep smoke probe < 1 GPU-hour where possible — cost signal is often sufficient to drop bad candidates early.
- Use embedding-similarity + two human-checked examples as a pragmatic quality gate for initial onboarding.
- Capture a minimal set of artifact metadata (quant config, group size, calibration seed) so we can re-run exactly later.

Risks / gotchas observed:
- Conversion scripts with non-deterministic layer orderings caused tiny diffs that made smoke probe results noisy. Fix: pin converter to commit and add a hash check.
- Some public toolchains re-order bias quantization and cause small but meaningful logits shifts. Note in playbook.

Appendix (quick references):
- Quick commands used during smoke: 
   * python -m quant_tools.convert --model rwd-llm-13b-v2 --group-size 128 --out /tmp/q.ckpt
   * python -m evals.quick_probe --model /tmp/q.ckpt --prompts tiny_eval.json --batch 2 --seq 64 --out smoke_report.json
- Slack thread: #applied-ml (links to run outputs pinned)

Status: saving as a draft — want feedback from Jonah and Maya before making canonical.

--- end of sketch ---
